title: The Quiet P
kidRule: P can be a hider too! At the very start of some words that came from Greek, P stays quiet before S, N or T, as in PSALM, PNEUMONIA and PTERODACTYL. It also hides in the middle of RASPBERRY and CUPBOARD, right before the B!
hint: A quiet letter is hiding in this word. We do not say it at all, and it sits right before a B, an S, an N or a T. Which letter is it?
reminder: A quiet P is hiding here: right before the B (P-B), or at the very start before S, N or T.

check.question: Why can't we hear the P in CUPBOARD?
check.correctAnswer: P stays quiet when it sits right before the B, and the B does the talking!
distractors: Because the letter U makes every P quiet
Because long words never say all of their letters

words.def: A small, soft, red fruit that grows on a prickly bush.
words.sent: I put one raspberry on top of each cupcake.
words.story: Each one of these fruits is really a bunch of about 100 tiny juicy beads stuck together, and every bead has its own seed!
words.card: The *raspberry* told the blue*berry* a joke so funny that it turned purple!

words.def: A piece of furniture with doors and shelves, where you keep things like plates and food.
words.sent: The cookies are on the top shelf of the cupboard.
words.story: Hundreds of years ago, this was just what its name says: a board, or table, where people set out their cups!
words.card: A tea*cup* hid in the *cupboard* and jumped out to shout 'Boo!'

words.sent: The choir sang a psalm at the start of the service.
words.story: This word comes from an old Greek word for a song that was sung while someone played the harp!
words.card: The c*alm* llama hummed a *psalm* to the sleepy sheep!

words.def: A flying reptile with big skin wings that lived long ago, in the time of the dinosaurs.
words.sent: A pterodactyl glided over the ancient sea.
words.story: The name means 'wing finger' in Greek. Each wing was a sheet of skin stretched along one very, very long finger!
words.card: The *pterodactyl* tried to *act* like a chicken, but nobody was fooled!

words.def: The study of the mind and of how people think, feel, and act.
words.sent: My aunt studies psychology to learn how memory works.
words.story: The first part of this word comes from 'psyche', the Greek word for the mind or the soul!
words.card: In *psychology* class we found out why *cho*colate makes everybody smile!

words.def: An illness in the lungs that makes a person cough and feel very tired.
words.sent: Grandpa rested in bed until his pneumonia was gone.
words.story: This word comes from 'pneumon', the Greek word for a lung. That is why it starts with such a strange pair of letters!
words.card: The *mon*key with *pneumonia* stayed in bed and sipped warm banana soup!

words.def: Any one of the flying reptiles that lived in the time of the dinosaurs.
words.sent: The museum has a pterosaur hanging from the ceiling.
words.story: The biggest pterosaur of all had wings more than 30 feet across. That is as wide as a small airplane!
words.card: The *pterosaur* gave a dino*saur* a piggyback ride to the moon!

words.def: A person who studies how people think and feel, and who helps them with their feelings.
words.sent: The psychologist asked the children how they solved the puzzle.
words.story: A famous psychologist named Jean Piaget found out how children think by watching and talking with children, including his own three!
words.card: The *psychologist* asked the *log* how it felt, and it said, 'A little board.'

words.def: A made-up name that a writer uses instead of a real name.
words.sent: The author wrote her first book under a pseudonym.
words.story: Dr. Seuss is a pseudonym! The real name of the man who wrote 'The Cat in the Hat' was Theodor Seuss Geisel.
words.card: Dr. *Seu*ss is a *pseudonym*, so now my goldfish signs his name as Sir Bubbles!

words.def: Filled with air, or made to work by air that is pumped or squeezed.
words.sent: The pneumatic pump filled my bike tire in seconds.
words.story: Long ago, big cities sent letters whooshing through pneumatic tubes under the streets, pushed along by air!
words.card: The door*mat* rode a *pneumatic* tube all the way up to the roof!
